functions.name: pf
functions.signature: pypsa.Network.pf(snapshots=None, skip_pre=False, x_tol=1e-06, use_seed=False, distribute_slack=False, slack_weights='p_set')
functions.description: Runs the full non-linear AC power flow on every sub-network of the model, solving the coupled active/reactive balance with a Newton-Raphson iteration for each snapshot. It fills the time-dependent result tables in place (bus voltage magnitudes and angles, branch active and reactive flows, slack-generator dispatch) and returns a dict of per-sub-network convergence diagnostics. By default only the slack generator absorbs the power mismatch, but distribute_slack spreads it across generators according to slack_weights.

parameters.name: snapshots
parameters.description: Subset of n.snapshots to solve; defaults to all snapshots.

parameters.name: skip_pre
parameters.description: Skip the preliminary topology / dependent-value / bus-control computation (only safe if already done).

parameters.name: x_tol
parameters.description: Convergence tolerance for the Newton-Raphson iteration.

parameters.name: use_seed
parameters.description: Warm-start the Newton-Raphson from the existing voltage guess instead of a flat start.

parameters.name: distribute_slack
parameters.description: If True, distribute the slack power across generators instead of assigning it all to the slack bus.

parameters.name: slack_weights
parameters.description: Scheme for splitting distributed slack: 'p_set', 'p_nom', 'p_nom_opt' or an explicit per-sub-network dict.

return_info.description: Dict with keys 'converged', 'error', 'n_iter', each a DataFrame indexed by snapshot x sub_network giving the Newton-Raphson outcome.

functions.name: lpf
functions.signature: pypsa.Network.lpf(snapshots=None, skip_pre=False)
functions.description: Runs the linearised (DC-type) power flow on every sub-network, holding voltage magnitudes at their nominal per-unit value and solving only for bus voltage angles from the reactance-weighted network. Active branch flows are then obtained linearly from the angle differences, ignoring resistive losses and reactive power. Being a single linear solve it always 'converges', which makes it the fast transmission-planning analogue of a DC power flow; results populate the same p0/p1 and v_ang result tables in place.

parameters.name: skip_pre

functions.description: Builds and solves the linear optimal power flow / capacity-expansion problem for the network using linopy, minimising total system cost (marginal generation cost plus annualised capital cost of extendable assets) subject to nodal balance, branch linear-flow limits, storage dynamics and any global constraints. On success it writes the optimal dispatch, extendable capacities (p_nom_opt / s_nom_opt), nodal marginal prices and the objective value back onto the network. transmission_losses adds a piecewise-linear loss approximation, and linearized_unit_commitment enables the relaxed on/off formulation.

parameters.name: transmission_losses

parameters.name: linearized_unit_commitment

parameters.name: solver_name

functions.name: global_constraints_mu
functions.signature: n.global_constraints.mu  # Series indexed by constraint name; shadow price
functions.description: The shadow price (dual value) of each global constraint after optimize. Global constraints impose system-wide limits such as a CO2 emission cap (carrier_attribute='co2_emissions'), and their mu is the marginal system-cost change per unit relaxation of the cap, i.e. the implied carbon price. return_info.description: Float Series indexed by global-constraint name giving the constraint's shadow price (e.g. CO2 price).
